Hi Samir — great to meet you and the team today. Appreciate the clear goals; below is a proposed POC plan and next steps. I attached a short POC plan (redwood-poc-plan.pdf) with timeline and responsibilities.

POC objective and success criteria (recap)
- Validate latency: median generation <=200ms on 2k context runs (target 99th pctl <400ms).
- Validate cost: target token cost <$0.0008/token for inference at expected load.
- Validate quality: automated eval set passes our agreed thresholds (ROUGE and manual Likert spot checks).

Proposed evaluation plan (2-3 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep): exchange sample payloads, share dataset, confirm success thresholds, set up monitoring hooks. (Owner: Acme — Samir; Redwood owner: Marissa + Neha)
- Week 1: Run baseline on Redwood hosted trial (no VPC) — measure latency/cost/quality.
- Week 2: If isolation/latency needs warrant, run on dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool) and/or VPC-hosted trial; compare numbers and recommend final config.
- Final week: wrap-up report and recommendation.

Environment options (short)
- Hosted trial (fastest): no infra changes; Redwood-managed endpoints. Good for quick baseline and quality checks.
- Dedicated sandbox: reserved capacity (predictable throughput), good if you need sustained concurrency and lower variance. Setup takes 3-5 business days to provision.
- VPC trial: customer-managed networking, best for security/regulatory requirements. Lead time ~7-10 business days depending on network approvals. Requires network contacts on your side to open firewall/route rules.

Ownership and contacts
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) — program lead / timeline, Neha (SE) — technical setup and validation, Rishi (CS eng) — performance/config tuning as needed.
- Acme AI: Samir — technical owner; Priya — procurement/security contact.

2) Redwood to provision a hosted trial env and share endpoints + monitoring dashboard (ETA: 1 business day after dataset received).
3) Depending on results, discuss dedicated sandbox or VPC trial in the follow-up call.

Hi Samir — adding a few technical notes to help you decide between hosted / dedicated / VPC: 

Hosted trial
- Pros: fastest to spin up (same-day), zero network config, Redwood-managed metrics and tracing, best for early quality/latency baselines.
- Cons: shared infra (multi-tenant), slight variance in tail latency under noisy neighbors.

Dedicated sandbox
- Pros: reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput, lower tail-latency variance. Supports longer sustained throughput tests.
- Cons: provisioning lead time (3-5 business days), requires capacity commit for sandbox period.

VPC-hosted trial
- Pros: private networking, suitable if you must keep traffic within your VPC or meet stricter compliance.
- Cons: requires firewall rules, allowlist of Redwood egress IPs or private endpoints, and possible changes to your routing (we can provide a CloudFormation/terraform snippet). Lead time typically 7-10 business days.

Network checklist for VPC
- Open outbound to Redwood-managed endpoints: TCP 443 to 52.34.10.0/24 (example) and 3 other CIDR blocks we will provide.
- Allow DNS to resolve internal endpoints; configure NAT/egress through approved gateways.
- If using PrivateLink, we will coordinate account IDs and required role setup.

Monitoring and metrics
- We will provide a monitoring dashboard with per-route latency, token counts, and cost burn. We recommend instrumenting a small subset of requests with response traces for quality sampling.

Attachments
- network-reqs.xlsx (sample firewall rules and example terraform snippet).

If your primary objective is to get baseline numbers quickly, start with the hosted trial. If you already have strict networking or compliance requirements, plan for VPC from the outset and we can accelerate approvals once we have the network contact.

I can be on the kickoff call and own the setup work for hosted + dedicated options. If we move to VPC, we'll loop in our infra team (timeline dependent).
